chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said:

There is no dying person to whom death comes except that Allah restores to him some of his hearing, sight, and intellect for the bequest, whether he makes the bequest or leaves it. This is the relief that is called the relief of death, and it is a duty upon every Muslim.

key_terms.حَقٌّ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ: an established duty upon every Muslim
key_terms.رَاحَةُ الْمَوْتِ: the relief associated with the approach of death
key_terms.سَمْعِهِ وَبَصَرِهِ وَعَقْلِهِ: his hearing, sight, and intellect restored at death

ai.seo_question: Why is making a bequest at the time of death considered a duty in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that when death approaches, Allah grants the dying person enough restored awareness to make a bequest. The hadith emphasizes both a divine mercy at the moment of death and the importance of the waṣiyyah as a right and duty for every Muslim.
